propositions: Repository documentation and comments must conform to a formal prose standard that prohibits em dashes, en dashes, spaced hyphens, semicolons, certain colons, contractions, colloquialisms, and designated filler terms.

Documentation ownership, lifecycle, and validation require a documented policy that distinguishes ADRs, internal current-state records, external user guidance, and developer comments by their intended audience and canonical source.

Three shards of documentation require separate exploration and filtered validation: durable records plus internal documentation, external documentation plus shipped help, and developer comments plus embedded prose.

Maintained prose surfaces across Markdown, help text, package metadata, YAML, TOML, HCL, shell, workflows, and schema descriptions require source-aware validation tooling that fails on deterministic prohibited forms and flags meaning-sensitive candidates.

A complete remediation register of 49 proposals (F01 through F49) addresses false guidance, missing user discovery, audience defects, maintainability issues, and bounded cleanup organized by priority level P0, P1, and P2.

Generated artifacts including configuration references, ADR indexes, CLI references, MCP descriptions, and templates require recorded canonical sources, regeneration contracts, and ownership before substantive changes.
